prompt.context: Our client is Bosch, a German household appliance company. They are known for their high-quality, German-made washing machines. Bosch is thinking of expanding into the Chinese market with their washing machines, specifically in Shanghai. They have hired us to find out if they should, and if so, how they should do it.
prompt.question: Should Bosch enter the Shanghai washing machine market? If so, how? Begin by estimating the market size and opportunity.

clarifying_info.q: What segments of the washing machine market are we considering?
clarifying_info.a: There are three sub-markets: residential (in-home), laundromats, and commercial (e.g., hotel basements). Bosch is not looking at the commercial market, so focus on in-home and laundromats.

clarifying_info.q: What is the population of Shanghai?
What price is Bosch planning to sell the machines at?
How many people are in a typical household?
How do people in Shanghai currently do their laundry?
clarifying_info.a: Assume an even split: one-third use in-home machines, one-third use laundromats, and one-third wash by hand. That is 6 million people (1.5 million households) for each option.

clarifying_info.q: How often do households visit the laundromat?
How many washing machines are in a laundromat?
How many loads does a family wash per laundromat trip?
How long does one load take?
How many hours per day is a laundromat open?
Does Bosch already have a sales network in China?
clarifying_info.a: This is an open question for the candidate to raise; the interviewer should let the candidate explore whether existing sales infrastructure exists or would need to be built.

exhibits.shows: The opening page of the case containing the case stem and Phase 1 instructions
exhibits.data: Population of Shanghai: 18 million; 4 people per household; even split among in-home, laundromat, and hand-washing

framework: Segment the washing machine market: in-home residential, laundromats, commercial (Bosch excludes commercial)
Estimate total addressable market for each relevant segment (population-driven sizing)
Calculate annual revenue opportunity per segment accounting for replacement cycles
Assess costs and operational challenges: shipping, manufacturing location, sales infrastructure
Evaluate marketing approach for each customer segment (residential vs. laundromat owners)
Synthesize into a go/no-go recommendation with key risks

questions.prompt: Estimate the total in-home washing machine market opportunity in Shanghai (annual revenue in dollars).
questions.guidance: Candidate should derive number of in-home households (18M people / 4 per household * 1/3 = 1.5M households), multiply by price ($400), then apply a replacement cycle assumption (every 5-10 years). Strong candidates note that not all 1.5M households need a machine today; replacement cycle drives the annual figure.

math.setup: Total in-home households = 18M / 4 * (1/3) = 1.5M. Annual revenue = (1.5M * $400) / replacement years.
steps: 18,000,000 people / 4 people per household = 4,500,000 total households
math.answer: ~$60 million per year from the residential in-home market (using a 10-year replacement cycle).

questions.prompt: Estimate the total laundromat washing machine market opportunity in Shanghai (annual revenue in dollars).
questions.guidance: Candidate should determine how many families each laundromat can serve per week, derive the number of laundromats needed to serve 1.5M households, multiply by machines per laundromat, apply a shorter replacement cycle (laundromats run machines constantly), and compute annual revenue. Strong candidates note the shorter lifespan vs. residential.

math.setup: Capacity per laundromat per week → number of laundromats → total machines → annual purchases → revenue.
steps: Families served per laundromat per hour: 20 machines / 3 loads per family (at 1 load/hour) ≈ 6.67, round to ~7 families/hour
Families per week: 7 families/hour * 10 hours/day * 7 days/week = 490, round to 500 families/week/laundromat
Number of laundromats needed: 1,500,000 households / 500 families per laundromat = 3,000 laundromats
Annual machine purchases (3-year replacement cycle): 60,000 / 3 = 20,000 machines/year
math.answer: ~$8 million per year from the laundromat market.

questions.prompt: What are the key challenges and positives Bosch would face entering the Shanghai market?
questions.guidance: Candidate should raise shipping costs (heavy machines, Germany to China distance), brand dilution risk if manufacturing locally, sales network (existing vs. greenfield), and market characteristics (rapid city growth, growing wealthy class, but also large poor population and apartment wiring constraints).

questions.prompt: How should Bosch market its washing machines if it decides to enter Shanghai — for both residential customers and laundromat owners?
questions.guidance: Residential: leverage German engineering reputation, target growing middle/upper class, highlight quality and reliability. Laundromat owners: emphasize durability, lower total cost of ownership over commercial lifespan, after-sales service. Candidate should distinguish the two customer segments' motivations.

brainstorming.prompt: What are the challenges and positives Bosch faces in entering the Shanghai washing machine market?

categories.name: Logistics & Supply Chain
ideas: Washing machines are very heavy; shipping costs from Germany to Shanghai are high
Long lead times due to distance
Need for reliable local distribution and last-mile delivery

categories.name: Manufacturing & Cost
ideas: Building a local plant in China reduces shipping costs but is expensive for an uncertain venture
Local manufacturing risks diluting the 'German engineering' brand value proposition
Variable labor and input costs in China

categories.name: Sales & Distribution
ideas: Does Bosch have an existing sales network or presence in China?
Building a sales force and retail relationships from scratch is costly and time-consuming
Potential to partner with local distributors or retailers

categories.name: Market Characteristics
ideas: Shanghai is growing rapidly — rising middle class increases addressable market over time
Large proportion of poor residents limits near-term market size
Apartment wiring or space constraints may limit in-home machine adoption
Laundromat segment may be more immediately accessible

categories.name: Brand & Marketing
ideas: Bosch brand is not established in China; awareness-building requires investment
German quality is a differentiator but may command a premium that limits volume
Competing against established local Chinese brands with cost advantages

recommendation: Bosch should likely NOT enter the Shanghai washing machine market at this time
Total annual market opportunity is modest (~$68M combined) given Shanghai's large low-income population and the logistics complexity of shipping heavy machines from Germany
risks: High shipping and logistics costs erode margins significantly
Establishing brand recognition in a new market is expensive and uncertain
Building a local plant to solve logistics would dilute the German-engineering value proposition
Strong local Chinese competitors with lower cost structures
next_steps: Conduct detailed cost analysis including shipping, tariffs, and distribution to assess true margin
Evaluate whether existing Bosch China infrastructure (for other product lines) could reduce sales setup costs
Assess feasibility of licensing or joint-venture arrangement that preserves brand while reducing logistics cost
Monitor Shanghai market growth — re-evaluate in 3-5 years as middle class expands
